<header>[Chapter 94] Chapter on the Cries of the Crow</header>

### Now, he explains the specific details—

> **The circle of directions is divided into thirty-two parts; whatever has been specified therein,**
> **that same result—whether good or bad—should be applied to those desiring to travel. ||49||**

In the circle of directions, which is divided into thirty-two sections, whatever fruit or result has been stated in whatever manner, that result should be declared in that very same way as the merit or fault for those who are "desirous of going" <note>original: "yiyāsūnām" — travelers or those planning a journey</note>. For example: if the crow makes a favorable gesture in a "peaceful" <note>referring to a specific ritual orientation of the compass</note> eastern direction, it indicates great results such as honor or worship. If it makes an unfavorable gesture in that same spot, the result is mediocre. If it is in a "blazing" <note>diptā — a direction associated with the sun's current position or ill omens</note> eastern direction and makes a cruel gesture, it indicates fear of the king. The same logic should be understood for the other directions as well. ||49||

### Now, he explains the results of specific vocalizations—

> **The sound "Kā" from a crow staying in its own nest is said to be fruitless.**
> **The sound "Kava" is for one's own pleasure; in the sound "Ke," there is the gain of a dear friend. ||50||**
> **"Kara" causes a quarrel; "Kuru Kuru" brings joy; and "Katakaṭa" means a meal of curd-rice.**
> **The cry "Keke" or "Kuku" tells of the gain of wealth for the traveler. ||51||**

Regarding the cry of the <term>Crow</term> <note>Sanskrit: vāyasa or kāka</note>: when the crow is situated in its own dwelling or nest and makes the sound "Kā," it is declared to be "fruitless." This means it carries no specific good or bad omen. The cry "Kava" results in personal satisfaction or "self-love." In the cry "Ke," there is the "attainment" or meeting of a "dear" or beloved friend. ||50||

In the cry "Kara," there is a "quarrel" or strife. In the cry "Kuru Kuru," there is joy. The word "atha" here serves as a conjunction. In the cry "Katakaṭa," there is a meal of "curd-rice" <note>a traditional auspicious food in India</note>. In the cry "Keke" or the cry "Kuku," it "tells" or predicts the "gain of wealth" or acquisition of money for the "traveler" <note>one who is currently moving</note>. ||51||

### He says something further—

> **"Kharekha" tells of the arrival of a traveler; "Kakhākha" tells of death for the traveler.**
> **"Ā" is a prohibition of departure; "Kakhala" is for immediate rain. ||52||**

In the cry "Kharekha," the crow "tells" or announces the "arrival" of a <term>Wayfarer</term> <note>Sanskrit: pathika — a traveler or guest coming from afar</note>. In the cry "Kakhākha," it speaks of "death" or passing for the traveler. The cry "Ā" acts as a "prohibition of departure," meaning it creates an obstacle to going. The cry "Kakhala" is for "immediate rain," meaning it will rain on that very same day. ||52||

# In the Brihat Samhita with Commentary [Chapter 94]

### He says another thing—

->**The sound "Kaka" indicates destruction, while "Kakati" foretells the spoiling of food.**<-
->**"Kavakava" is a source of affection, and "Kagaku" indicates imprisonment. ||53||**<-

When the crow cries "Kaka," there is destruction or ruin. When it cries "Kakati," they say it foretells the spoiling or poisoning of food <note>The commentator suggests this could refer to the presence of poison or other impurities in a meal</note>. When it cries "Kavakava," it is a "source of affection"—meaning it is a place or occasion for love; one develops a friendly bond with someone. Others read the phrase "affection for a couple" <margin>Alternative reading: "Kavakava" refers to the affection between a husband and wife.</margin> for "Kavakava." This would mean a husband and wife, out of love and affection, make the sound "Kavakava." This interpretation is not ideal. Because Garga <note>An ancient sage and authority on astrology and omens often cited by Varahamihira</note> says:

->When a crow makes the sound "Kavakava" while one is departing,<-
->It should be pointed out as a sign of unprecedented affection and the gain of wealth.<-

Likewise, when the cry is "Kagaku," there is "bondage," meaning imprisonment or being tied up. ||53||

### He says another thing—

->**The sound "Karagau" brings rain; "Guda" is for alarm; "Vang" brings the acquisition of clothes.**<-
->**The sound "Kalayati" brings the union of a Shudra with Brahmins. ||54||**<-

When the cry is "Karagau," there is a shower of rain. "Guda" leads to alarm or fear. When the cry is "Vang," there is the gain of garments or a benefit of wealth. When the cry is "Kalayati," there is a "union"—a meeting or association—of a Shudra <note>The laboring class in the traditional social structure</note> with Brahmins <note>The priestly or scholarly class</note>. ||54||

### He says another thing—

->**The sound "Kad" brings the attainment of fruit; "Tadd" brings the sight of a fruit-giving snake or blows.**<-
->**The gain of a woman comes from the cry "Stri";**<-
->**"Gad" is for cows, and "Pud" is for flowers. ||55||**<-

When the cry is "Kad," there is the "attainment of fruit," meaning the achievement of a desired result. Or, it simply means the gain of actual fruit. Likewise, there is the "sight of a fruit-giving snake" <note>The text prints 'varshanam' (showering), likely a typo for 'darshanam' (seeing), as confirmed by the following explanation.</note>—the seeing or beholding of a snake that bestows auspicious results. Alternatively, "attainment of fruit" means a constant gain; "fruit-giving" means it bestows an even more specific or superior result.

# Chapter on the Cries of Crows

<page-num>191</page-num>

Thus, the observation is as follows: If the crow makes the sound *Tang*, there will be strikes or physical assaults. If it cries *Stri*, there is the gain of a woman <note>original: "stri-labha"; likely referring to marriage or a female servant</note>. If it cries *Gad*, there is the gain of cattle. If it cries *Pud*, there is the gain of flowers. ||55||

->He says something further:<-

->**The cry "Taku-Taku" portends war; "Guhu" indicates fear of fire; "Kate-Kate" means a quarrel.**<-
->**The sounds "Takuli," "Chinit-chi," and "Ke-ke-ke" regarding a town are for evil/misfortune. ||56||**<-

The cry *Taku-Taku* is for war or battle. If it cries *Guhu*, there is fear of fire. The cry *Kate-Kate* results in a quarrel. The cries *Takuli*, *Chinit-chi*, and *Ke-ke-ke* directed toward a town are for misfortune. ||56||

->He mentions a further distinction:<-

->**This result, which has been stated through cries and movements,**<-
->**is the same for two crows as well.**<-
->**So it is for other birds, and for wild animals like dogs,**<-
->**and those who have upper tusks. ||57||**<-

Whatever result was stated for a single crow based on its cry or its movement (such as where it sits), the same should be declared for two crows. By the use of the word "as well" <note>original: "api-shabdat"</note>, the same applies to three or four crows. Other birds not specifically mentioned here should be understood in the same manner. Wild animals (those living in the forest) not previously mentioned should be interpreted like dogs <note>original: "shvavat"; following the omens prescribed for dogs</note>. Those with upper tusks, such as boars and similar creatures, also share the results stated for dogs. As the sage Parashara says:

> "Male-named birds are explained by the rules for the Crow;
> Likewise, female-named birds are explained by the rules for the Pipili <note>The Common Woodcock or a specific female bird</note>." ||57||

->Now he describes the movements of other creatures:<-

->**The reversal of land and water creatures during the rainy season**<-
->**indicates abundant rain; at other times, it indicates fear.**<-
->**Honey found settled in a house quickly makes it empty (deserted),**<-
->**and a blue fly settling on the head brings death. ||58||**<-

During the "cloud-season" (the monsoon), a reversal <note>original: "vyatyaya"</note> of land and water creatures occurs. When land-dwellers (like goats) act like water-dwellers, or water-dwellers (like fish) come onto land, it portends abundant rainfall. In the remaining seasons (other than the monsoon), such a reversal leads to fear. Land—

# In the Brihat Samhita with Commentary [Chapter 94]

The reversal of the natural behavior of aquatic creatures leads to fear <note>indicating impending danger or misfortune</note>. By the word "honey," honeybees and flies are meant. If honey is found clinging or attached to a house of its own accord, it quickly makes that house empty and deserted. If a blue-colored fly clings to the head of a living being, it even causes death. || 58 ||

### On the behavior of ants:

-> Ants casting away their eggs in water <-
-> indicate the obstruction of rain. <-
-> When they carry them from low ground to a tree or high ground, <-
-> then they foretell rain. || 59 ||

Ants casting away their eggs in water indicate the obstruction of rain—meaning a lack of rainfall. If they carry them from low ground to a tree or a high place, then those ants foretell or speak of rain—meaning a downpour. || 59 ||

### Now, on the determination of omens:

-> One should know the result of the primary omen for the task; <-
-> for an intermediate omen, the result occurs on that very day. <-
-> Thus, these should be considered. At the start of works, at the time of journey, <-
-> and likewise at the time of entry, a sneeze is to be noted; <-
-> they say it is never auspicious. || 60 ||

The "primary omen" <term>mula-shakuna: the first omen encountered when starting an endeavor</term> is the first omen. Regarding that, one should know the outcome of the task or journey. If that omen is auspicious, the journey will be successful; if inauspicious, it will fail. Regarding "intermediate omens on that day": after the traveler encounters the primary omen and until the completion of the journey, any other omen—auspicious or inauspicious—that occurs in the interval or middle is an "intermediate" omen. One should know that its fruit or result occurs on that very day. These omens mentioned in this chapter are to be considered and reflected upon at all times: at the commencement of all works, at the time of departure on a journey, and likewise at the time of entering a house and so on. In all these tasks, omens must be considered. Likewise, a sneeze <note>literally "the sound of the nose"</note> must always be taken into account. The meaning is that after hearing a sneeze, no work should be undertaken. For they say it is not auspicious anywhere; a sneeze is inauspicious in all circumstances. || 60 ||

### To praise these very omens, he says:

-> Good fortune, the ripening of one's period, success without obstacles, <-
-> the protection of one's capital, or the arrival of helpers... <-

<header>[Chapter 94] Chapter on the Detailed Behavior of Crows</header>

->**They speak of the successful conquest of the wicked and freedom from disease**<-
->**For the King who honors them. || 61 ||**<-

Those omens speak to the King who honors them—that is, the one who respects and worships them. They announce a favorable outcome, the ripening of good fortune, and the accomplishment of tasks without obstacles (<term>avighna-siddhi</term>: success achieved without hindrance). They also signify the protection of the "root" (<note>original: "mūla"; refers to the capital city or the foundation of power</note>), or for one traveling on a road, they signify helpful companions. Furthermore, they foretell the easy conquest of a wicked or difficult enemy and a state of being free from disease. All of this is communicated through these auspicious signs. || 61 ||

### Now, he describes what must be done if an unfavorable omen's cry is observed:

->**Some say an omen’s cry is fruitless beyond a distance of two miles;**<-
->**If the first omen is unfavorable, the King should perform eleven breath-controls.**<-
->**If the second is inauspicious, sixteen;**<-
->**But if a third is unfavorable, he should return to his own palace. || 62 ||**<-

Some teachers, such as Kashyapa and others, have stated that an omen's cry occurring beyond a distance of one <term>krosha</term> (<note>approximately 2 miles or 3 kilometers</note>) is "fruitless" or without effect. As Kashyapa says:

> Whatever occurs beyond a distance of one krosha, whether auspicious or inauspicious,
> that movement of the omens should be understood as having no result.

Thus, what is heard within the distance of a krosha is fruitful, and beyond that, it is fruitless. However, this is not the opinion of the [current] Author. Regarding the phrase "If the first omen is unfavorable": if the first omen encountered at the time of starting a journey is inauspicious, the King, with a steady and pure mind, should perform five and six—meaning eleven—<term>pranayamas</term> (<note>yogic breath-control exercises</note>).

### Now, he defines the characteristics of breath-control (Pranayama):

->**Reciting the Gayatri mantra with the sacred utterances, the syllable Om,**<-
->**And the "Head" mantra three times while holding the breath is called Pranayama.**<-

The <term>vyahritis</term> (sacred utterances) are seven: *Om Bhuh, Om Bhuvah, Om Svah, Om Mahah, Om Janah, Om Tapah, Om Satyam*. The <term>pranava</term> is the syllable *Om*. The "Head" (<note>shiras</note>) refers to the mantra: *Apo jyoti raso'mrtam...* (<note>Water, light, essence, the immortal...</note>). The <term>Gayatri</term> is the well-known twenty-four syllable prayer. One who is "holding the breath" has suspended their breathing. One should recite this three times. If the second omen is inauspicious, one should perform sixteen breath-controls. Then—

->Now, the "Supplement on Omens" is explained.<-

# The expert in cries should announce the results after considering the direction, the place, the movement, the sound, the day, the lunar mansion, the Muhurta, the Hora, the Karana, and the rising sign and its divisions. ||1||
# He must also understand the relative strength or weakness of the moveable, fixed, and mixed signs. ||1||

The **direction** refers to the East and so forth <unclear>as well as the intermediate points</unclear>. The **place** refers to the location, whether it is auspicious or inauspicious. **Movement** refers to the physical activity or behavior of the creature. **Sound** refers to the cry, whether it is "blazing" <note>dipta: harsh or alarming</note> or "peaceful" <note>shanta: calm or favorable</note>. The **day** refers to the specific weekday and its auspicious or inauspicious nature based on planetary movements. The **lunar mansion** <term>Nakshatra: the 27 divisions of the sky</term> refers to the categories of fixed, soft, sharp, swift, fierce, mobile, or ordinary. The **Muhurta** refers to the specific 48-minute intervals of the day, such as the one dedicated to Shiva. The **Hora** refers to the half of a zodiac sign or the planetary hours, relating to whether they belong to a benefic or malefic planet. The **Karana** refers to the half-tithi <note>lunar day</note> such as Bava, whether auspicious or inauspicious. The **rising sign** is the Ascendant. The **divisions** refer to the sub-sections of a sign, including the Decan <term>Drekkana: 10-degree division</term>, the ninth-part <term>Navamsha</term>, the twelfth-part, and the thirty-degree divisions. Furthermore, the **moveable** signs are Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn. The **fixed** signs are Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius. The **mixed** or dual-natured signs are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces. Having understood the relative strength and weakness of these omens and zodiac signs, the "expert in cries"—one who understands the meaning of animal sounds—should announce the results. ||1||

Now, to demonstrate the types of events, he says:

# For those situated in a place, they say the effects are of two kinds: the "Incoming" and the "Stationary."
# These include matters regarding kings, messengers, spies, things from foreign lands, accidents, and the arrival of one's own kin. ||2||

For men situated in a particular location, they declare that the effects of omens are of two types. What kind? The "Incoming" and the "Stationary." "Incoming" refers to the future. "Stationary" refers to the present or the past. Likewise, they speak of other matters arising from kings, messengers, spies, and foreign lands. A "king" is the ruler; a "messenger" is a traveler or envoy; a "spy" is the well-known secret agent. "Foreign land" refers to another country. They describe events arising from these. Likewise, "accidents" refer to calamities or injuries. They also declare the "arrival" <note>Agama</note> of one's own people, such as relatives and friends, and the specific name of the person who has arrived. ||2||

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of omens (Shakuna), specifically focusing on how to determine if a predicted event is fixed (already happening/past) or moving (yet to occur in the future).</meta>

<page-num>195</page-num>
# Chapter on the Higher Knowledge of Omens
<meta>[Chapter 95]</meta>

## Now he describes the knowledge of fixed and moving events—

-> Being bound, union, eating, thieves, fire, <-
-> rain, festivals, the birth of a son, death, strife, and fear. <-
-> This group is considered "fixed" when the rising sign and the Moon are in fixed signs; <-
-> know that in "moving" signs, the same events are considered "moving." ||3|| <-

"Being bound" means being attached or staying in one place, devoid of coming and going. "Union" refers to sexual enjoyment with someone. "Eating" is the act of consuming food. "Thieves" are robbers. "Fire" is a conflagration. "Rain" is the act of raining. "Festivals" include marriages and similar celebrations. "The birth of a son" refers to a male child. "Death" is the end of life. These, as well as "strife" (meaning a riot or tumult <note>original: "damara"</note>) and "fear" (terror). This group is "fixed." One should see that the word "if" is implied here. If this group arises from a fixed location or is indicated by an omen situated in a fixed place, it is then known as <term>Fixed-Signification</term> <note>The text uses "charasamjnah" here, but the context of the commentary implies the fixed nature of the omen's result.</note>. This is what is meant: if these actions are indicated by an omen through the behaviors previously mentioned or those yet to be described, this is stated to determine whether these events have already occurred or are yet to come. Regarding "when the rising sign and the Moon are in fixed signs": if this group is fixed, and the rising sign (Ascendant) is a fixed zodiac sign, and the Moon is also joined with a fixed sign, then one should know that the event is currently happening on that very day, or has already happened. If the rising sign is a "moving" sign (cardinal sign), the Moon is in a moving sign, and the omen is situated in a moving place, then all the aforementioned things like "being bound" etc., should be known as "moving," meaning they will happen in the future. ||3||

## Now he describes the characteristics of fixed and moving locations—

-> In fixed places, on stones, in houses, in temples, and near earth or water, <-
-> actions are fixed; those in moving places and the like are for future arrival. ||4|| <-

"Fixed place" means a stable location; motionless. "Stone" means a rock. "House" means a dwelling. In these places. "In temples" means the house of a god. "Near earth or water" means on the ground or in the vicinity of water. In these places, the omens indicate that the results (good or bad) are fixed. Those omens which are in "moving places"—meaning on moving creatures or, by the use of the word "and the like," on moving grass, wood, and so on—those are "moving." They are for "arrival," meaning they will occur in the future, specifically by the end of the current fortnight. ||4||

## Now he describes the knowledge of rain—

-> In watery signs, at watery times, in watery directions, or in water, <-
-> those omens that cry out while "blazing" <note>A technical term for omens facing the sun or in a harsh direction.</note> at the end of a fortnight, <-
-> all of them are rain-makers; <-
-> even a water-dwelling bird, when "calm," produces rain. ||5|| <-

# In the Brihat Samhita with Commentary [Chapter 95]

The "watery" signs are Cancer, Capricorn, and Pisces. The watery constellations are Purva Ashadha and Shatabhishak. The watery <term>Muhurta</term> <note>a unit of time approximately 48 minutes long</note> is that named after Varuna (the god of waters). The watery direction is the West. A watery place is any location where water is present. If portents or omens—whether natural, divine, or caused by specific actions—occur in these watery signs, constellations, times, directions, or locations, or if they occur at the end of a lunar fortnight (the New Moon or Full Moon), and if the creatures are crying out or shrieking, they all without exception bring rain. Even a water-dwelling bird, if it is in a "calm" state but situated in these watery locations, indicates that rain is coming. ||5||

### Now, the knowledge of the danger of fire is described:

->If a bird, inflamed by the sun, cries out in the direction,<-
->ascendant, time, or place associated with fire, it portends fear of fire.<-
->So too if it cries during the <term>Vishti</term> <note>an inauspicious astrological timing</note>, or during the<-
->ascendant of Saturn’s signs, or on thorny trees or leafless creepers.<- ||6||

The "fiery" direction is the South-East. The fiery ascendants are the cruel signs, namely Aries, Leo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Aquarius. The fiery <term>Muhurta</term> is the one named after Agni (Fire). The fiery constellation is Krittika (the Pleiades). A fiery place is anywhere fire is present. If a bird "inflamed by the sun" <note>meaning facing the sun or in a state of agitation caused by solar heat</note> shrieks in these places, it leads to a fear of fire. Regarding "Vishti": this refers to the Vishti <term>Karana</term> <note>a division of the lunar day</note>. "Yama" refers to Saturn; his signs are Capricorn and Aquarius. When these are rising, or if the bird is perched on thorny trees or leafless vines, an "inflamed" bird causes harm or misfortune. ||6||

### Now, the knowledge of strife/quarrels is described:

->If a domestic bird, agitated in its voice and gestures,<-
->shrieks fiercely while perched on a thorny tree,<-
->and if the ascendant is a sign of Mars, and the bird is in the South-West,<-
->or seen directly in front or on both sides, it portends a quarrel.<- ||7||

A "domestic" bird is one born in a village. If it is "inflamed" by its voice or its physical movements—meaning it is making harsh sounds or agitated gestures—and is shrieking fiercely while perched on a tree with thorns; and if the <term>Lagna</term> (ascendant) is one of the signs of Mars (Aries or Scorpio); and if that bird is situated in the South-West direction; and if it is seen directly in front or on both the left and right sides, it results in a quarrel. ||7||

### Now, the gathering/collection of omens is described:

->If the ascendant or the Moon is in a sign or division of Venus,<-
->and the bird cries while facing downwards in an intermediate direction...<-

### Now, he describes the outcome of actions through another method:

**At the commencement of all undertakings, one should count from the sign occupied by the Sun to the Ascendant.**

When beginning any work or action, one should count from the sign where the Sun <note>original: "Arka" (the Sun)</note> is situated up to the current Ascendant sign. The first sign (where the Sun sits) is "Success" <note>original: "Sampat"</note>, the second is "Misfortune" <note>original: "Vipat"</note>, the third is "Success," and so on in sequence. Regarding the blindness of the eye: if one wishes to know the appearance of the person arriving, and the Sun is in the twelfth house from the current Ascendant, that man arrives blind in the right eye. If the Moon is in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, he is blind in the other (left) eye. <margin>The text suggests that the physical traits observed at the moment of an omen mirror the birth chart of the person involved.</margin>

# Chapter on the Sequel to Omens
### Chapter 15

Thus: If both the Sun and the Moon are in the twelfth house <note>The house of loss and the subconscious</note>, the person is blind. If the Sun is in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> and is aspected <note>seen</note> by the two malefics, Mars and Saturn, the person is blind or lacks eyes. If the Sun is in its own sign <note>Leo</note> in the Ascendant, the person becomes a hunchback, lacks hearing (deaf), or is dull-witted (a fool). ||12||

"A malefic in the sixth," etc.: If a malefic planet—any one of the Sun, Mars, or Saturn—is in the sixth house from the specific Ascendant, and if that malefic is also aspected by another malefic, then a wound or scar should be predicted on the limb corresponding to that house. The specific limb is determined by the "Limb of Time" <note>Kalapurusha: the concept of the zodiac as a human body</note> as stated in the text beginning with "The limbs of Time are the head," etc. In this manner, all signs, marks, forms, and shapes mentioned at the time of birth <insert>the nativity</insert> should be considered in this section. For example: "If Mercury is in a trine and others are weak, the person has double the usual number of faces, feet, or hands." Also:

->If Saturn and Mars are in a sign or division of a benefic, the child is born with teeth.<-
->If the Moon is in its own sign in the Ascendant and aspected by Saturn and Mars, one is a hunchback.<-
->If Pisces is the Ascendant and is aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and Mars, one is lame.<-

->If the Ascendant is the end of Capricorn and is aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, one is a dwarf.<-
->If the fifth, ninth, or first houses are occupied by Decans <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</term> joined with malefics, one may be without arms, feet, or a head.<-
->If the Sun and Moon are in Leo in the Ascendant aspected by Mars and Saturn, one is sightless; if aspected by benefics, the eyes are merely protruding like bubbles.<-
->The Moon in the twelfth house destroys the left eye, and the Sun there destroys the right; these malefic yogas <note>astrological combinations</note> become manageable if aspected by benefics.<-

And so on. Likewise, everything mentioned in the "Chapter on Unfavorable Combinations" should be considered. ||13||

<header>In the Brihat Samhita with Commentary [Chapter 95]</header>

### **I shall now declare the names, divided according to the sequence of the centers, as composed by the sages. ||1||**

Following this knowledge of inquiry, I shall describe the names well-known among the people, which are a collection of various letters representing substances—whether minerals, plants, or living beings <note>The commentator refers to the three categories of matter: dhatu (minerals), mula (roots/plants), and jiva (living souls)</note>. These names were composed and established by the "desired ones"—the authoritative sages such as the Greeks <note>original: "Yavana"</note>, Arka, Vasistha, Parasara, Maya, and others. I shall state these names, which have been categorized and defined, according to the sequence of the "centers" <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a horoscope</term>. ||1||

->Regarding the knowledge of this sequence, he says:<-

### **From the signs and portions of signs located in the Ascendant, the Fourth, the Seventh, and the Tenth houses, one should determine the letters associated with their own houses, following the sequence of the planets' own groups. ||2||**

"Located in the Ascendant" means in the first house. "Located in the Water" means in the fourth house. "Located in the Setting" means in the seventh house. "Located in the Sky" means in the tenth house. In these "fields" or zodiac signs, one looks at the portions of the signs <note>original: "grihamsha," referring to the Navamsha or ninth-part divisions</note> that are present. From these portions of the signs—the ninth-parts of Aries and the others that are situated in the eastern horizon and the other centers—one should know the letters that reside in their own houses. That is, the letters whose source or location is that specific house, according to the sequence of the groups belonging to the planets, starting with the Sun and the others. ||2||

->Now he states the groups of the planets:<-

### **They say the groups beginning with 'Ka' belong to Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn respectively. The letters beginning with 'Ya' are assigned to the Moon, and the letters originating from 'A' belong to the Sun. ||3||**

The sages declare the groups of letters, starting with the "Ka-group" <note>The Sanskrit alphabet is organized into phonetic blocks</note>, in the order of the planets starting with Mars. Specifically:
The **Ka-group** (k, kh, g, gh, ṅ) belongs to Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note>.
The **Ca-group** (c, ch, j, jh, ñ) belongs to Venus <note>original: "Shukra"</note>.
The **Ṭa-group** (ṭ, ṭh, ḍ, ḍh, ṇ) belongs to Mercury <note>original: "Candri," son of the Moon</note>.
The **Ta-group** (t, th, d, dh, n) belongs to Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva"</note>.
The **Pa-group** (p, ph, b, bh, m) belongs to Saturn <note>original: "Arkaja," son of the Sun</note>.
The eight letters beginning with **Ya** (y, r, l, v, ś, ṣ, s, h) are said to belong to the Moon.
The letters that have **A** as their origin or first member belong to the Sun. These are the vowels: a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, e, ai, o, au, aṃ, aḥ.

# Chapter 15: The Chapter on the Results of Omens
<note>Original title: Śakunottarādhyāyaḥ</note>

The Sun's letters are the vowels. The letters **ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa** belong to Mars. **Ca, cha, ja, jha, ña** belong to Venus. **Ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa** belong to Mercury. **Ta, tha, da, dha, na** belong to Jupiter. **Pa, pha, ba, bha, ma** belong to Saturn. **Ya, ra, la, va, śa, ṣa, sa, ha** belong to the Moon. (3)
<note>This system maps the Sanskrit alphabet (varga) to the planets to determine the starting letter of a person's name or a query.</note>

->Now he explains the knowledge of the number of letters in a name based on the Zodiac Signs and the Decans:<-

> By the increase of the Decans <term>Drekkāṇa: a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign, also known as a decan</term>, they say a name has
> Three, five, or seven letters in an odd-numbered sign.
> In an even sign, one should know it has two, four, or six
> Letters in the name, increased by the aspect of the planets. (4)

A Decan is a third part of a Zodiac sign. By its "increase" (progression), in an odd-numbered sign <term>Oja-rāśi: Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</term>, a name has three, five, or seven letters. In the first Decan, it is three letters; in the second, five letters; and in the third, seven letters. If an even-numbered sign <term>Yugma-rāśi: Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc.</term> is ascending, one should know the name has two letters in the first Decan. In the second, four letters. In the third, six letters. These letters of the name are further influenced by the "increase of the planetary aspect" <term>Dṛṣṭi: the 'glance' or astrological aspect one planet casts upon another</term>. Since the letters are derived from the signs situated in the cardines <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>. Because the four cardines are under discussion, this science is indeed drawn from two types of combinations. One is the combination by position, and the second is the combination by aspect. Setting aside the combination by position, they are derived here by the combination of aspects. In the combination of aspects, there is a consideration of strength and weakness. As it has been said:

> They look at the third, tenth, trine, square, and seventh houses with an increase of a quarter-foot.
> Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—and the others—
> Respectively become more powerful in their viewing. <margin>1. This is from the Bṛhajjātaka, Chapter 2, Verse 13.</margin>

In this way, the number of letters in the names are derived through the increase of the planetary aspects. (4)

->Now he explains the knowledge of the number of letters in a name based on the Ninth-Part division:<-

> In the Best-Division <term>Vargottama: a planet occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the 9th-part chart, considered very strong</term>, there are two letters in a movable portion.
> In a fixed sign portion, it has four letters.
> In odd signs, there are an odd number of letters from these,
> But in dual-natured signs, it is like the Zodiac sign itself. (5)

"The Best-Divisions are the first, middle, and last portions of the movable, fixed, and dual signs respectively." <margin>2. This is from the Bṛhajjātaka, Chapter 1, Verse 14.</margin> Thus the Ninth-Part divisions <term>Navāṃśaka: a 3°20' division of a sign</term> called "Best-Divisions" are described. Because of the use of the word "odd" later on, it is understood here to refer to even signs. In an even sign, when there is a Best-Division in a movable portion (such as Cancer or Capricorn), then the name has two letters. In a fixed sign portion...

# Commentary on the Great Compilation [Chapter 95]

When the <term>Vargottama</term><note>The best division; specifically when a planet or the rising sign occupies the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth-division/Navamsha chart.</note> is a <term>Sthira-amsha</term><note>A fixed portion/degree</note> in any of the signs Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, then the name consists of four syllables. In the odd signs, such as Aries or Libra, if these <term>Vargottama</term> portions are present, the syllables in the name will be of an odd number. This is what is meant: when the <term>Vargottama</term> is a <term>Chara-amsha</term><note>A movable portion</note> in an odd sign, there should be three syllables in the name. However, if the <term>Vargottama</term> is a fixed portion in that same sign, then there should be five syllables in the name. In the "dual-natured" signs, it is according to the sign itself; in the dual-natured or "double-bodied" ascendants, it should be equal to the nature of the sign. This is what is meant: in the dual-natured signs of Gemini or Sagittarius, if the <term>Vargottama</term> is an odd portion, the name has three or seven syllables. If the <term>Vargottama</term> portion is even in the dual-natured signs of Virgo or Pisces, then the name has four or six syllables. As it is said:

->One should know three, five, or seven syllables in an odd sign; in an even sign, two, four, or six.<-
->One should speak according to which <term>Drekkana</term><note>A ten-degree subdivision of a sign; a decan.</note> the <term>Vargottama</term> portion is situated in. ||5||<-

Regarding this, he mentions a specific detail:

->In a "double-bodied" sign, one should predict a double name,<-
->And also in a dual-natured sign if it is aspected by Mercury.<-
->As many groups of portions as have passed at the time of rising,<-
->That many is the collection of syllables in the name. ||6||<-

In a "double-bodied" or dual-natured sign, one should state a "double name"—that is, a person who has two names. Likewise, in a dual-natured sign aspected by Mercury <note>original: "Saumya-ikshite"</note>, because of the word "and," one should also predict a double name. Whatever the quantity or group of <term>Navamshas</term><note>Ninth-parts of a sign</note> that have passed at the time of the query, that same number represents the collection of syllables or letters in the name. ||6||

Now, he speaks of the compound consonants:

->One should know a conjunct consonant at the beginning in odd signs;<-
->In "sharp" signs, they say the conjunct consonant comes later.<-
->In its own exalted portion, a letter is doubled; from the union of stars,<-
->A heavy syllable occurs in the portion of a heavy planet. ||7||<-

In the "many" or odd signs, one should know that the <term>Samyoga</term><note>A conjunct or compound consonant, like 'kt' or 'str'.</note> occurs at the very beginning of the name. A conjunct consonant is the joining of two sounds. Some define it as "consonants without intervening vowels" <note>original: "halo'nantarāḥ saṃyogaḥ"</note>. There are many varieties: some are doubled, some are "heavy" (long vowels), and some are doubled because they precede a conjunct. For example—

<vocab>Vargottama (best division), Sthira-amsha (fixed degree), Dvisvabhava (dual-natured sign), Drekkana (decan), Saumye-kshite (aspected by Mercury), Samyogakshara (conjunct consonant), Halo'nantarah (consonants without vowels), Ojarashi (odd-numbered sign)</vocab>

# Chapter on Omens and Answers
<page-num>1003</page-num>

->**Chapter on Omens and Answers**<-

Yappa, Valla, Yassa, Lassa. Heavy syllables <note>term: Guru (heavy/long syllable)</note> are formed in two ways: by letters of the same class <note>term: Varga (consonant groups in Sanskrit phonology)</note> and by their own bodies <note>doubled letters</note>. By the first with the first; the third with the third; the fifth with the fifth. Examples of the first with the first: *Kakka*, *Datta*, *Kutta*. Examples of the third with the third: *Lalla*, *Gagga*, *Dadda*, *Jajja*. Examples of the fifth with the fifth: *Shankha*, *Nanna*, *Dhamma*. By another body, with the first and second, and the third and fourth. Examples of the first and second: *Khukkha*, *Ichcha*, *Vittha*. Examples of the third and fourth: *Vaggha*, *Daddha*, *Shuddha*. These are heavy syllables. Others are formed by another body: the fifth with the first, the fifth with the second, the fifth with the third, and the fifth with the fourth. These are simply conjunct consonants <note>term: Samyoga (clusters of consonants)</note>. Examples of the fifth with the first: *Shad-ngka*. Fifth with the second: *Shankha*. Fifth with the third: *Shringam*. Fifth with the fourth: *Sangha*.

Some explain it differently, saying: conjuncts with their own bodies are also called "doubled." For example: *Dhamma*, *Datta*, *Kakka*. The conjunction of the first with the second and the third with the fourth are called heavy syllables. Other designations are not considered conjuncts, such as: *Dharma*, *Vatsa*. Examples of initial conjuncts: *Shridhar*, *Kshira*, *Smara*. Thus, one should know the abundance of conjuncts at the beginning. In "Kuta" <note>cryptic or complex astrological calculations</note>, they speak of following conjuncts. In even signs <note>term: Samara-shi (even-numbered zodiac signs like Taurus or Cancer)</note>, they speak of following conjuncts. Narayana and others say a "following conjunct" is that which has a conjunct consonant coming after it. In a two-syllable name, examples are: *Padmam*, *Dharma*, *Vatsa*, and so on. In a four-syllable name: *Vasudatta*, *Vasugupta*, and so on. In its own highest degree <note>term: Svoccha-amshaka (the specific degree of a planet's exaltation)</note>, it is doubled. "Its own" refers to that highest degree.

> The Sun and others are exalted in Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, Pisces, and Libra.
> Their degrees of exaltation are ten, three, twenty-eight, fifteen, five, twenty, and ten respectively; their points of fall are the same degrees in the opposite signs. <note>original: "Aja-vrishabha-mrigangana..." This is a famous verse from the Brihat Jataka 1.13</note>

In that highest degree of exaltation, a letter in the name becomes doubled. "Doubled" means performed twice. How? Through the conjunction of the lunar mansion <note>term: Riksha</note> or the conjunction of the zodiac sign. The planet that grants the letter, when situated in its highest degree, makes the letter doubled. This is what is meant: if the rising sign of the query <note>term: Prichcha-lagna</note> is an odd sign, then the odd-positioned letter is doubled, such as: *Darada*, *Damodara*. If it is an even sign, then the even-positioned letter is doubled, such as: *Devadeva*, *Dharadhara*. In two-syllable names: *Kappa*, *Yappa*, *Valla*, and so on. A heavy syllable occurs in its house-division. In whichever name there is a heavy syllable, that is the "heavy-syllable name." By "that," the rising sign is referred to. It is the division of that house. When that letter is present, it should be said that a heavy syllable occurs. This operates through the conjunction of the lunar mansions and so on. In an odd sign, only an odd letter becomes a heavy syllable: *Kapitthya*, *Ashvatthya*. In an even sign, only an even letter: *Khukkha*, *Ghaggha*, *Shuddha*. In four-syllable names: *Shuddhodana*, and so on. ||7||

# In the Great Compilation with Commentary [Chapter 95]

He mentions another specific detail:

->The vowel marks and other features are linked to the planets in the trines,<-
->following the sequence of the decans <note>original: "drekkana"</note> among the letters.<-
->When the sky-points are strong, the marks are above; when the water-points are strong, they are below;<-
->the aspiration <note>original: "visarga"</note> is known when the setting-point is endowed with strength. ||8||<-

In the trine—meaning the ninth or fifth house—from the rising sign <term>Prashna-lagna; the zodiac sign ascending on the eastern horizon at the moment of the query</term> such as Aries and others, as the conjunction with planets like the Sun occurs, so shall the vowel marks <term>matra; the symbolic strokes representing vowels in the Sanskrit script</term> be applied. First, the conjunction occurs with the vowel marks of the name. For example: *Shiva*. Regarding the phrase "following the sequence of the decans among the letters": the sequence of the decans refers to their established pronunciation. As that sequence is, so is the application of vowel marks among the letters. In even-numbered decans, the vowel marks apply to even-numbered letters. In odd-numbered letters, for example: *Shridhara*. In even ones, for example: *Ishvara*. Regarding "when the sky-points are strong, the marks are above": those signs that are strong in the sky—the tenth house—are called "sky-strong." And thus it is said:

<margin>1</margin>
> Human-shaped signs are strong in the ascendant; four-footed signs are strong in the middle <note>the 10th house</note>;
> Water-dwelling signs are strong in the water-point <note>the 4th house</note>; the Scorpion is strong in the setting-point <note>the 7th house</note>; and double-bodied signs are strong in the sky-canopy.

Furthermore:

> 'The terms "Thorn," "Center," and "Four" refer to the seventh, first, fourth, and tenth houses.
> In those respective places, the Scorpion, Humans, Water-dwellers, and Animals are considered powerful.'

Among those, when the sky-points are strong, they declare the vowel marks are above the letters. For example: *Shrivatsa*, *Vasudeva*, *Vaishravana*, *Shaunda*. Regarding "when the water-points are strong, they are below": when the fourth house is powerful, the vowel mark is below the letter. For example: *Suhiranya*, *Shuravarma*. Regarding "the aspiration is known when the setting-point is endowed with strength": when the seventh house is powerful, the aspiration <note>the "h" sound represented by two dots in Sanskrit</note> is to be understood. ||8||

He says another thing:

->In signs that rise head-first, they desire the vowel mark above;<-
->and below in those called hind-rising.<-
->One should know it is horizontal in those that rise both ways;<-
->long in long signs, and otherwise in others. ||9||<-

<note>1. This is verse 17 of Chapter 1 of the Brihat Jataka.</note>

# Chapter 15: The Chapter on Omens and Answers

<page-num>1095</page-num>

**Head-rising** means those signs that emerge from the horizon head-first. And so it has been said:

> The human forms and the lion <note>Leo</note> and the insect <note>Scorpio</note> are described by the Greeks <note>original: "Yavanas"</note> as head-rising. The two fish <note>Pisces</note> are inclined both ways, while the remaining signs always rise by the back.

And also:

> "Aries, Taurus, Sagittarius, Cancer, and Gemini, along with Capricorn, are known as night-signs; these same ones, excluding Gemini, are said to be **back-rising**. The remaining signs are **head-rising** and possess strength during the day. The pair of large-scaled fish <note>Pisces</note> approaches the ascendant <term>Lagna: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term> from both sides."

Thus, in the case of **head-rising** ascendants, they desire or declare the vowel marks to be placed *above* the letter. For example: *O* (ओ) and *Au* (औ). In those signs designated as **back-rising**, they declare the vowel marks to be placed *below*; for example: *U* (उ) and *Ū* (ऊ). And "transversely" as well: Pisces is **both-ways-rising**, and in that sign, one should understand the vowel mark to be placed transversely or across. For example: *E* (ए) and *Ai* (ऐ), as in the words *Devadeva* or *Aindra*.

Regarding "long marks for long signs": in the **long** (extended) signs, one should understand the vowel mark to be long. For example: *Ā, Ī, Ū, E, Ai, O, Au*. In the others—the **medium** and **short** signs—one should understand the remaining marks to be **short**. For example: *A, I, U*. Here, the long signs are Leo, Virgo, Libra, and Scorpio. The medium signs are Gemini, Cancer, Sagittarius, and Capricorn. The short signs are Aries, Taurus, Aquarius, and Pisces.

And so it has been said:

> The duration of the rising of the first and last signs is fixed at two <term>Muhurtas: a unit of time approximately 48 minutes</term> each. The duration of the rising of the two halves of the zodiac should be known by regular and reverse order until the fifth sign. In this way, the houses <note>signs</note> are understood to be short, medium, or long. Having been made equal to the divisions of the limbs of the cosmic cycle, they also determine the measures of the paths.

And also:

> "In the first half, the measures are five-fold and so on, and the reverse in the second half." (9)

He states a specific rule on this very subject:

-> From the signs situated in the Ascendant, the Fourth, the Seventh, and the Tenth houses, <-
-> the collection of letters is derived based on the degrees. <-
-> A malefic planet situated in these four houses destroys a letter; <-
-> if situated in a trine <note>the 5th or 9th house</note>, it destroys the vowel mark even if it only casts an aspect. <- (10)

<page-num>1006</page-num>
<header>In the Great Compilation with Commentary [Chapter 95]</header>

The "Ascendant" refers to the sign rising in the east. The "Water-sign" refers to the fourth house. The "Setting" refers to the seventh house. The "Sky-sign" refers to the tenth house. These are the signs situated in these specific positions. By the word *Bha*, the zodiac signs are meant. From the <term>Navamshas</term><note>The ninth part of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuned predictions</note> or sub-divisions of those signs situated in such positions, the collection of letters or the assembly of sounds in a name is derived. "A cruel planet destroys a letter": a cruel or malefic planet situated in the <term>Kendras</term><note>The four central pillars of a horoscope: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> strikes out or removes a letter. That same malefic planet, if situated in a <term>Trine</term><note>The 5th or 9th houses, considered auspicious positions</note>, destroys a vowel or a measure of sound merely by its aspect (vision). "In the ninth or fifth is the Trine." The word "and" implies a combination, while the word "or" implies an alternative. ||10||

### He states another specific rule—

> A benefic planet, possessing great strength,
> Is said to grant letters equal to its position and division.
> Whether aspecting or situated in a Kendra or Trine,
> Or in its exaltation, it grants two letters if in its own division. ||11||

A "benefic planet" means a gentle or auspicious one. The word "but" is used for emphasis. Such a planet possesses "great strength"—that is its nature. It is a "giver of letters equal to its position and division." In whichever house and in whichever numerical <term>Navamsha</term> it is situated, it grants a corresponding number of letters. Thus, it is described as a giver of equal letters. "Whether aspecting or situated": alternatively, that same benefic planet, possessing great strength, situated in the <term>Kendras</term> or the <term>Trines</term> (the ninth or fifth), or aspecting them; or situated in its own sign of exaltation, or aspecting its own <term>Navamsha</term>, grants two letters. The word "also" indicates an alternative possibility. ||11||

### He states another specific rule—

> When the Lord of the House and the division are weak,
> The vowel and letter produced from them meet destruction.
> Even if impossible, it comes into existence in that case,
> The first of the group, if joined with an exalted division or seen by its Lord. ||12||

When the "Lord of the House" (the ruler of the Ascendant) is "weak in power" (depleted of strength) and in a "weak division" (a weak ninth-part), the "vowel and letter produced from it" meet destruction. "Vowel and letter" refers to the components of the name. "Produced from it" means born from that planetary position. It "meets destruction" or undergoes decay. "Even if impossible": in that same case where the Lord and its division are weak, the destruction of that vowel or letter is reversed and it "comes into existence" or attains manifestation. What comes into existence? The "first of the group" (the first letter of a consonant class). Under what conditions? When it is "joined with an exalted division" (situated in its highest point) or "seen by its Lord" (aspected by the ruler of that sign). ||12||

# On the Determination of Uncertainties—

->Having understood the excellence of the strength of the position<-
->of the zodiac sign and its lord within the center,<-
->one should perform the sequential joining of letters<-
->and the arrangement of vowel-marks and combinations. (13)<-

In the center <note>Sanskrit: *kendra*; refers to the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope</note>, meaning in any one of the ascendant, fourth, seventh, or tenth houses. Of the sign, meaning the zodiacal constellation. And of its lord, meaning the owner of that sign. The excellence of the strength of the position: "position" and "strength" are positional strengths, and their "excellence" is their superiority. The first letter is obtained through positional strength, and the second and subsequent letters through aspectual strength <note>the influence planets have by "looking" at one another</note>. Having understood this, then the sequential joining of letters <note>Sanskrit: *varna*; the individual sounds of the alphabet</note> must be performed. The joining should be done in the proper order. Likewise, the arrangement of vowel-marks <note>Sanskrit: *matra*; the strokes indicating vowels like 'i', 'u', 'e', 'o'</note> and combinations must be done. "Vowel-marks and so on" refers to the arrangement of combinations starting with vowel-marks, including initial and final combinations. This is what is meant: the bottom-marks, top-marks, and side-marks <note>referring to how Sanskrit vowels are written around a consonant</note> are to be applied through the arrangement of combinations. (13)

## Now he describes the letters of the zodiac signs according to the sequence of the divisions—

->There, beginning with the first sign and the four cardinal points,<-
->following the sequence of the first divisional parts,<-
->this attainment of the letters of their own groups<-
->from the planetary divisions should be maintained for the sake of meaning. (14)<-

There, in that process of bringing forth the name. Beginning with the first sign: the first sign is Aries, and starting with that, the four cardinal points <note>Sanskrit: *catur-vilagna*</note> known as Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn. Following the sequence of their first divisional parts <note>Sanskrit: *navamsha*; the 1/9th sub-division of a sign</note>, according to the arrangement of the first sub-divisions, this attainment or production of the letters of their own groups—meaning the letters prescribed for the groups of the nine planets—should be performed. This is established by the rule: "The groups starting with 'Ka' belong to Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn" <note>original: *kavarga-pūrvān kuja-śukra-cāndri-jīvārkajānām*</note>. (14)

## Now he states the letters according to the sequence of the first sign and others—

->In Aries is the letter 'Ka'; in the Fourth House <note>Sanskrit: *hibuka*; a term derived from Greek 'hypogeion'</note> is 'Ya';<-
->In Libra is 'Ca'; in Capricorn is 'Pa'.<-
->In Aries is 'Cha'; in the Fourth House also is 'A';<-
->In Libra is 'Kha'; in Capricorn is 'Pha'. (15)<-

# From the Great Compilation with Commentary [Chapter 95]

When Aries is the rising sign <note>the Ascendant</note>, the signs situated in the centers <note>the four cardinal houses or 'Kendras'</note> are Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn. These signs rise according to their own portions <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning astrological predictions</term>. 

In this arrangement, the first ninth-part of Aries is Aries itself, and its ruler is Mars. Because it is the first ninth-part of Aries, the first letter from the group of Mars <note>the 'ka-varga' or velar consonants</note> is assigned: the letter **Ka**. 

In the fourth house <note>called 'Hibuka' in Sanskrit, derived from the Greek 'hypogeion'</note>, Cancer is situated. Its ruler is the Moon. Since its first ninth-part is rising, the first letter from the group of the Moon <note>the semi-vowels</note> is assigned: the letter **Ya**. 

In the seventh house, Libra is situated. Its ruler is Venus. Because it is the first ninth-part, the first letter from the group of Venus <note>the palatal consonants</note> is assigned: the letter **Cha**. 

In the tenth house, Capricorn is situated. Its ruler is Saturn. Because its first ninth-part is rising, the first letter from the group of Saturn <note>the labial consonants</note> is assigned: the letter **Pa**. 

Therefore, it is said:

->In Aries, the letter **Ka**; in the fourth house, **Ya**; in Libra, **Cha**; and in Capricorn, **Pa**.<-

In the same way, for the second and subsequent ninth-parts, one should select the letter corresponding to the number of the ninth-part by following the sequence of the groups assigned to the ruling planets. For the enlightenment of those with a simple intellect, we shall demonstrate this further:

For the second ninth-part of Aries, Venus is the lord; from that group, the second letter, **Cha**, is assigned. For the second of Cancer, the Sun is the lord; from that group, the first letter, **A**, is assigned. For the second of Libra, Mars is the lord; from that group, the second letter, **Kha**, is assigned. For the second ninth-part of Capricorn, Saturn is the lord; from his group, the second letter, **Pha**, is assigned. 

Therefore, it is said:

->In Aries, the letter **Cha**; in the fourth house, **A**; in Libra, **Kha**; and in Capricorn, **Pha**. || 95 ||<-

He further describes the others:

> In Aries, the letter **Ta**; in the fourth house, **Tha**;
> In Libra, the letter **Ta** <note>dental</note>; in Capricorn, **Tha** <note>aspirated dental</note>.
> In Aries, the letter **Ra**; in the fourth house, **Ja**;
> In Libra, the letter **Ba**; in Capricorn, **Ga**. || 16 ||

For the third ninth-part of Aries, Mercury is the lord; from his group, the first letter, **Ta** <note>retroflex</note>, is assigned. For the third ninth-part of Cancer, Mercury is also the lord; from his group, the second letter, **Tha** <note>retroflex</note>, is assigned. For the third ninth-part of Libra, Jupiter is the lord; from his group, the first letter, **Ta** <note>dental</note>, is assigned. For the third ninth-part of Capricorn, Jupiter is the lord; from his group, the second letter, **Tha** <note>dental</note>, is assigned. 

Therefore, it is said:

->In Aries, the letter **Ta**; in the fourth house, **Tha**; in Libra, **Ta**; in Capricorn, **Tha**.<-
